item.title: AP Top 25: After Week 9
item.description: SAN JOSE, CA - OCTOBER 31: New Mexico Lobos players make their way do to the field during the college football game between the San Jose State Spartans and the New Mexico Lobos on October 31, 2026, at CEFCU Stadium in San Jose, CA. (Photo by Samuel Stringer/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With the first College Football Playoff rankings set to be unveiled Tuesday night, this week’s AP Top 25 only gets about two days of relevance before it’s completely cast aside by media and fans. Still, it’s fun to see how things changed with a handful of upsets on Saturday. Let’s dive in. AP Top 25 Miami (FL) (62 first place votes) Georgia (7) Utah (1) Notre Dame UCLA Indiana BYU Kentucky Alabama Texas Ohio State Ole Miss Texas Tech Wake Forest LSU Tennessee Houston USC Missouri Boise State Iowa New Mexico South Carolina Arizona Florida Where is UNC? A near upset of top-ranked Miami wasn’t enough to get the Tar Heels any votes. Maybe if they had been able to finish the job… Biggest Winners Missouri had the biggest jump within the poll, rising four spots to #19 after a 34-10 win at Arkansas. Utah jumped three spots to #3 after a 49-25 win at Cincinnati – matching its highest ranking since 2015 – and UCLA moved up two spots to #5 after a 27-0 win over Nevada. It’s the Bruins’ highest ranking since 2001. New Mexico entered the rankings for the first time in its 135-year history at #22 after improving to 7-1 with a 21-16 win at San Jose State. Immediately behind the Lobos, South Carolina entered the rankings for the first time this season at #23. The Gamecocks improved to 5-3 with a 42-25 win at Oklahoma. USC and Iowa returned to the top 25 at #18 and #21 respectively. The Trojans beat then-#2 Ohio State (which was missing starting quarterback Julian Sayin) 30-18, while the Hawkeyes rolled then-#25 Wisconsin 30-0. Biggest Losers The loss at USC sent Ohio State tumbling nine spots to #11, the biggest drop within the poll. It’s the first time the Buckeyes have been ranked outside the top 10 since September 2021. Florida also had a major slide, dropping eight spots to #25 after a 27-8 loss to then-#3 Georgia in Atlanta. In addition to Wisconsin, SMU (previously #19), Northwestern (previously #20), and Oklahoma State (previously #24) dropped out of the poll after losing to unranked opponents. The Mustangs lost 30-27 at Syracuse on a last-minute touchdown, the Wildcats lost 34-26 at Oregon after leading 20-6 at one point, and the Cowboys lost 51-49 at Iowa State on a walk-off field goal. Northwestern is now the unofficial #26, SMU the unofficial #29, Oklahoma State received just three voting points, and Wisconsin did not appear on any ballots. item.description: Previous position previews: Point guards , Combo guards , Wings , Combo forwards The post position has been a bit of a revolving door for Mizzou during Dennis Gates’ tenure in Columbia. Noah Carter had a solid first season in Columbia before seriously regressing in year two, then his graduation gave way to a pair of one year transfers in Josh Gray and Shawn Phillips Jr. MU’s lack of an elite big man or the depth required to solve for that issue has been a sticking point for the Tigers the last few seasons, holding them back in a conference that has seen plenty of elite bigs recently. Gates responded this offseason with his strongest effort yet to find a more permanent solution at post, bringing in a pair of talented transfers with proven high major experience to bolster a room that also features an inexperienced but promising returner. Here is Mizzou’s group of posts for the 2026-2027 season: Trent Burns: 7-foot-5, 260 lbs., junior, Cypress, Tex. Jaylen Carey: 6-foot-8, 255 lbs., senior, Miami, Fla. Bryson Tiller: 6-foot-11, 245 lbs., sophomore, Atlanta, Ga. The Returner Trent Burns – The former four-star recruit’s first two years of his collegiate career featured plenty of twists and turns. Burns missed his freshman season with a foot injury and was not able to appear until Nov. 25 last year, when he made his Tigers debut against South Carolina State. He played sparingly for most of the season, averaging less than five minutes per game until a Feb. 18 matchup with Vanderbilt when he saw the floor for 17 minutes. Burns’ playing time, and production, took a major leap forward from that point on. He played nearly 15 minutes a game from that contest until the end of the season, averaging 3.4 points and 3.3 rebounds during that eight-game stretch. The Cypress, Texas, native’s impact dipped during the back half of those eight games, but he showed why he was a sought-after recruit in and also displayed the potential to play a more consistent role in the future. The Newcomers Jaylen Carey – The veteran journeyman might be the most underrated addition of Mizzou’s offseason. Carey was the sixth man for a Tennessee team that went to the Elite Eight last season, averaging 7.4 points and six rebounds a game. He also collected eight points and 5.7 rebounds per game the year prior at Vanderbilt, given him two proven seasons of production in the SEC — rare among transfers. Carey has also established a reputation as one of the game’s elite rebounders, ranking 10th nationally in offensive rebounding percentage (17.1%) last season and leading all SEC players in total rebounds during conference play during his year with the Commodores. That skill is especially valuable for a Tigers squad that has struggled heavily at times under Dennis Gates to hold its own on the boards. item.title: Compared to the Brewers, the Phillies don’t develop players
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WI - JUNE 13: Alec Bohm #28 of the Philadelphia Phillies throws the ball prior to the game between the Philadelphia Phillies and the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on Saturday, June 13, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kylie Bridenhagen/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images With the Brewers now crowned the champions of the baseball world, there has been a lot written about lessons to be learned from them and how said lessons could be applied to various team around the game. The Phillies have not been immune to this discussion as there have been a few think pieces about which ideas and/or practices they could adapt to how they have constructed their various rosters and what the Phillies could learn from that. It’s all well and good, but it sort of feels like an exercise in them trying to catch up. Instead, I wanted to take a different approach to this. Both the Brewers and Rays have reached the pinnacle of their leagues mostly because they have zagged where others have zigged philosophically, made good players even better with a successful player development system and eschewed the big move to continue making smaller moves that have paid off in a big way. One area that people always think that the Phillies could be better at is in the drafting of players. Had they drafted better players, they would now be in the position to stock a roster full of players capable of piling up victories. But what if I asked you this: what would you have done were you the Phillies? Would you have made the same moves that they did? If given the chance to draft a certain player based solely on a scouting report held in front of you, are you sure you’d take the same player that is on the roster of the current world champion? Thanks to the Baseball America archives, we can go back and look at scouting reports from when players had been drafted to see which player you would take were you in charge of making the final decision. I’ve edited a lot of this by blanking out names, positions, handedness if necessary and where the player was drafted from – college or high school. That way, you can’t just say, “Oh, that’s Player X, I’ll just take him.” I also promise you that all of these are accurate, straight from the pages of Baseball America. Outside of these minor edits, these were the actual scouting reports at the time of the draft. It’s a fun little game, so let’s play! item.title: This Week in Field Hockey: Kuiper Scores One, Sets Up One, and Rutgers Gets Indiana Again
item.description: No. 18 Rutgers took four shots in the first half against No. 15 Indiana on Friday and scored on two of them. They just took two in the second half. Indiana took seven, put six on goal, and Emily Nicholls saved all six. Rutgers won 2-1 at the Bauer Complex to finish the regular season 11-7 and 5-3 in the Big Ten, with wins in six of its last seven and a fourth ranked win. This column closed last week by asking what happens when Rutgers takes more than four shots of its own. It took six, and it won. The reward is the No. 4 seed and Indiana again, on Wednesday in Columbus. Three Substitutes and Three Minutes Indiana had the first quarter to themselves. Theresa Ricci was credited with their penalty corner at 2:22, and Mijntje Hagen’s shot off it was blocked 17 seconds later. At 6:38 Inés Garcia Prado made space in the circle and put a backhand past Nicholls, assisted by Berta Saenz de Santa Maria. It was her third goal of the season and Indiana’s first in three games. Ricci went wide at 8:17. Rutgers did not take a shot in the quarter. Indiana took three. Frederique Vernooij took Rutgers’ first shot 22 seconds into the second quarter, and Sadie Canelli saved it at 15:22. Sophie Kuiper went wide at 18:52. Then nothing for nine minutes, while Indiana did not take a shot of its own. At 26:49 Rutgers sent on three players at once. Olivia Stazi came on for Olivia Fraticelli, Laura Loycke for Talia Schenck and Kuiper for Caroline DeKenipp. Sixty-two seconds later this game was level. Stazi got a touch on the ball and Kuiper finished it at 27:51, with 2:09 left in the half. Ninety-nine seconds after that, Kuiper sent a bouncing pass through the middle, the ball got through several Indiana defenders and past Canelli, and Loycke touched it home at 29:30 with 30 seconds left before halftime. It was Loycke’s second goal in three games, after the one at Iowa. Three players came on at 26:49. All four Rutgers scoring points went to them, and the whole sequence took 161 seconds. Rutgers outshot Indiana 4-0 in the second quarter and went in ahead 2-1. Six on Goal, Six Saves Indiana came out of halftime with more of the ball and Rutgers kept the lead without adding to it. Nicholls saved Agustina Gamonal at 34:29. Hannah Riddle took a green card at 35:07, and Kuiper’s shot during the two minutes was saved by Canelli at 35:31. Nicholls saved Garcia Prado at 40:24. Rutgers took one shot in the third quarter, Indiana two, and both of Indiana’s were on goal. Nicholls saved Celia Arroyo Cabezudo at 45:44. Vernooij went wide at 49:02, and that was the last Rutgers shot of the game, with 10:58 still to play. Nicholls saved Hagen at 52:52. At 53:32 Indiana took Canelli off for an extra attacker, the third straight game it had gone to the empty net, and Karly Redman came on in her place. item.title: Raiders rally with resurgent 2nd half to ground Jets 38-33 in road win
item.description: (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images A tale of two halves. It’s a hackneyed description of sporting events in general, however, what occurred within the confines of MetLife Stadium in New Jersey between the visiting Las Vegas Raiders and the host New York Jets epitomized that classic phrase. Gang Green came out like gangbusters at home going 5-for-5 on each of its first-half offensive possessions to build a 23-14 advantage at halftime. And after Braelon Allen’s hard-charging 21-yard gallop in the third quarter, the Jets went an impeccable 6-for-6 with points scored after each of those drives orchestrated by offensive coordinator Frank Reich and quarterback (and former Raider) Geno Smith. The Silver & Black, meanwhile, produced just 103 yards on offense and a single touchdown — a ridiculous one-handed grab by tight end Brock Bowers — while reserve running back and dynamic kick return man Dylan Laube made a house call on a 95-yard kickoff return (the first of the 2026 NFL season, by the way) and only possessed the ball for 10:43 compared to the Jets 19:17 time of possession. But that Allen breakaway-touchdown was the last end zone visit for the Jets. The Raiders put forth an exhibition in complementary football in the second half going 3-for-3 on their offensive possessions to outscore New York 24-10 as the J-E-T-S, L-O-S-T a game in which they dominated in the first half. The Silver & Black’s display of resurgence and resilience (which had been lacking in the four-consecutive losses) produced a rally and a 38-33 Las Vegas win to snap the four-game slide and get the team back to .500 at 4-4 overall. “I thought halftime-wise, our guys (said), ‘We’re not happy,’” Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said after the game. “We made some adjustments and the guys just played harder. That just showcases the dramatic 180-degree turn the two teams did after trading touchdowns at the onset of the third quarter. “It’s just about taking a stand,” Raiders edge rusher Crosby said. “At some point it really comes down to winning your one-on-one’s and outworking the man in front of you. item.title: Sandy Alderson on Hall of Fame ballot for contemporary era
item.description: NEW YORK, NY - MARCH 29: General Manager Sandy Alderson of the New York Mets looks on before the game against the St. Louis Cardinals at Citi Field on Thursday, March 29, 2018 in the Queens borough of New York City. (Photo by Alex Trautwig/MLB via Getty Images) | MLB via Getty Images The National Baseball Hall of Fame has announced the candidates on the ballot for the Contemporary Baseball Era, and Sandy Alderson is among them. Alderson was at one time a private attorney before becoming general counsel to the then-Oakland Athletics in 1981. After two years in that role, he took Billy Martin’s spot as the general manager of the A’s, and built teams that reached the World Series in 1988-1990. They took home the pennant in 1990. During his first time with the Mets, Alderson was the executive vice president of baseball for Major League Baseball starting in 1998 and ending in 2005. He next took a job as CEO of the San Diego Padres until 2009. In 2011, he joined the Mets as their general manager. During his time with the Mets, he had a limited budget to work with. Nonetheless, Alderson made moves such as extending David Wright, trading for Zack Wheeler, and drafting Jacob deGrom. In 2015, the Mets made it back to the World Series, only to lose in five games to the Royals. However, Alderson was named Executive of the Year in 2015. He remained in his role as general manager with the Mets until 2018 After a brief return to the A’s, Alderson returned to the Mets as the team president when Steve Cohen purchased the team. He transitioned to an advisory role in 2022. His career in baseball has been long and storied, thanks to a high baseball IQ, good business sense, and probably vampires, and his nomination to the ballot is well deserved.

item.title: Former Houston Astros manager Dusty Baker up for Hall of Fame election on Contemporary Era ballot
item.description: Former Astros skipper Dusty Baker, who led a record five teams to the playoffs, is among eight former managers or executives on the Contemporary Baseball Era Committee's ballot. (Karen Warren/Staff photographer) Dusty Baker is one step away from the Baseball Hall of Fame. The former Houston Astros manager was among eight finalists - four former managers and four executives - announced on the Contemporary Baseball Era Committee's ballot announced Monday. Baker, 77, managed the Astros from 2000-03 and led the team to four playoff appearances and two World Series, winning it all in 2022 . He managed a record five different teams to the postseason (13 total appearances) during a 26-season career as a skipper. He was a three-time Manager of the Year (1993, 1997, 2000) and finished his career with 2,183 wins, eighth all-time, and one of just 13 men to reach 2,000 wins. ALSO SEE: Dusty Baker says he went against Astros brass' wishes during 2022 World Series run The other managers on the ballot are Bruce Bochy (Padres, Giants, Rangers);, Joe Maddon (Angels, Rays, Cubs), and Lou Piniella (Yankees, Reds, Mariners, Rays, Cubs). Bochy, who started his playing career with the Astros , won three World Series with the Giants (2010, 2012, 2014) and one with the Rangers (2023). Maddon and Piniella won championships with the Cubs (2016) and Reds (1990), respectively. Executives on the ballot are Sandy Alderson (A's, Padres, Mets); Brian Sabean (Yankees, Giants); Ted Turner (former Braves owner) and Bill White, the former president of the National League. A 15-member board will vote on the finalists, with candidates needing to be on 75 percent of ballots for election. The electees will be announced at 7 p.m. CT on Sunday, Dec. 6 at the winter meetings in San Diego, with MLB Network airing the announcement. For much of 2025, particularly at the end of the season with Brady Cook at quarterback, the Jets were a comedically mismatched bad team. They didn’t have the talent or the coaching necessary to be competitive with practically any of the other 31 teams. In 2026 the Jets are also a bad team, but they are a different type of bad. The talent level is better. Of course, that isn’t saying much. The Jets could be putting practically any sort of roster on the field and still be much better than what we saw at the end of last season. The 2026 Jets still rank fairly low on talent relative to the rest of the league. That is particularly true on defense. I’m not sure many of the players who took the field in yesterday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders would see much playing time on a Super Bowl caliber defense. Even most of those who would make the cut almost certainly would have smaller roles than they have with the Jets. There are any number of reasons the Jets are so low on talent on the defensive side of the ball. Teams do have to prioritize which areas they want to improve first in a rebuild, and the Jets have sunk many resources into their offense. Their frustration originated from comments Carragher made on a recent episode of 'Stick to Football', where he made it abundantly clear that Manchester United ranked above Villa in soccer's hierarchy and that their Spanish manager would entertain a move to Old Trafford. Virgil van Dijk slams controversial VAR decision as Liverpool narrowly lose to Arsenal Manchester United star set for 'a longer period' out as up to 13 players to miss Chelsea trip -Credit:Marc Atkins, Aston Villa FC via Getty Images "Surely he (Unai Emery) would want that opportunity to manage a giant again," Carragher said, as per The Mirror . "There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not. So Real Madrid will take Manchester United's best player, they'll take (Cristiano) Ronaldo. There's very few above United, same with Liverpool. "But there will be teams below Aston Villa, and they'll take their manager, or they'll take their players, so shut the **** up Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Man United." Carragher subsequently acknowledged his remarks and issued an apology over the weekend. He said: "I'd like to apologize to Aston Villa, the owners and their fans. My language this week was clumsy and wrong. I can assure Villa fans it was tongue-in-cheek, but I can understand it's not come across that way, so apologies." Villa have since withdrawn their threat of legal action against Carragher in the wake of his apology, according to BirminghamLive , though they insist such disparaging remarks will not be tolerated in the future. item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Minkah Fitzpatrick’s ‘Jets being Jets’ confession is damning for Aaron Glenn appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . One of the most entertaining games of the Week 8 Sunday slate in the NFL was surprisingly played between the Las Vegas Raiders and the New York Jets . There wasn’t much defense to speak of, but the Raiders eventually escaped with a 38-33 win to get to 4-4 on the season. On the other side, the Jets are now 2-6 after another frustrating loss and are quickly falling out of AFC playoff contention. The Jets had plenty of chances to win this game, but too many mistakes cost them in the end. After the game, star safety Minkah Fitzpatrick gave his take on what cost the Jets this game that included a stinging review of what the franchise has become, via Rich Cimini of ESPN. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I think we had some bad penalties, bad mistakes,” Fitzpatrick said. “Jets being Jets.” Indeed, the Jets finished with six penalties for 32 yards on Sunday. That’s not an astronomical number, but Las Vegas picked up two first downs off of penalties, so those calls came in some of the biggest moments of the game. But penalties are not at the top of the list for why the Jets ended up losing this game. The New York defense has no answer for Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers and the Raiders passing game in this one. Las Vegas finished with 238 passing yards on 8.8 yards per pass, and Bowers found the end zone two times in the win. The Jets have clearly improved from last season, and they are clearly a competent team this season. Some fans and pundits have used that as an endorsement of Aaron Glenn , citing that he has the franchise moving in the right direction even if some talent deficiencies catch up to them more often than not on game day. But Fitzpatrick’s “Jets being Jets” dig after losing on Sunday is an indictment on Glenn. New York continues to lose games based off of silly mistakes and a poor defense, which is supposed to be Glenn’s area of expertise. If it doesn’t get turned around, there could be a coaching search in the Big Apple this offseason. Related: Is Jets HC Aaron Glenn worried about getting fired as fan base gangs up on him? item.description: Should fantasy managers who drafted Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander be concerned? While the league's reigning Most Valuable Player is healthy, some of his key teammates couldn't avoid injuries that will sideline them for extended periods. As a result, SGA has been left to shoulder even more responsibility, leading a rotation that has become less experienced than it was on Opening Night. First, the Thunder lost Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/fibula) during the same game, an October 25 win over the Clippers, and they're not guaranteed to play again this season. That game is also the last time Chet Holmgren (knee) played, and he'll be out for at least 8-10 weeks. Lastly, Alex Caruso was sidelined by a sprained ankle suffered during an October 26 win over the Suns and has not played since. In Oklahoma City's last three games, Gilgeous-Alexander has averaged 24.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 0.7 steals, 0.7 blocks and 1.7 three-pointers per game, shooting 49.1 percent from the field and 85.7 percent from the foul line. Those certainly aren't "bad" numbers, but they aren't on par with what most fantasy managers expect from SGA when selecting within the first three or four picks of a draft. Can he continue to produce at a level that would align with his preseason ADP? And do the injuries in Oklahoma City open the door for Lakers guard Luka Dončić to crack the expected top three of Gilgeous-Alexander, San Antonio's Victor Wembanyama and Denver's Nikola Jokić (in no particular order)? It will be interesting to see how things play out for SGA, including whether or not the Thunder use some of their future draft capital to improve the roster. item.title: The Capitals Cannot Fit Dylan Larkin on Their Books
item.description: The Washington Capitals are one of the 10 teams on Dylan Larkin’s approved trade list, and the Detroit Red Wings have been doing their homework on them. Assistant general manager Kris Draper, who runs Detroit’s pro scouting, sat in the press box for two Capitals games in four days: Wednesday against the Philadelphia Flyers and Sunday against the Minnesota Wild. What Draper is looking at is not hard to guess. What is harder is figuring out how Washington could actually fit Larkin on its books. Oct 28, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Philadelphia Flyers goaltender Joseph Woll (53) makes a save on Washington Capitals left wing Ilya Protas (62) during the first period at Capital One Arena. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Cap Is the Hurdle in a Capitals-Red Wings Trade The piece Detroit wants is Ilya Protas. Alexander Rosquez of The Hockey Writers notes that TSN’s Pierre LeBrun has called the 20-year-old forward “an obvious target for Detroit in any package.” Protas put up 29 goals and 66 points in 69 games with the AHL’s Hershey Bears and was named the league’s rookie of the year. Here is the problem. Protas carries a cap hit of just $932,500 in each of the next three seasons, and Larkin’s cap hit is $8.7 million. Prospects and picks do not move that kind of money. For this to work, Washington has to send real salary back to Detroit. According to puckpedia.com , the Capitals have minus $1.32 million in projected cap space and $2.27 million in cap space. As for the Red Wings , they have $23.44 million in projected cap space and $28.42 million in cap space. Detroit has the room to absorb a contract. Washington does not have the room to add one. Dylan Strome Is the Obvious Salary to Send Back Rosquez does not name a cap casualty, but one name fits the math better than the rest. Dylan Strome carries a $5 million cap hit through the 2027-28 season. Moving him would clear most of the space Washington needs, and Detroit has the room to take him without sending anything back. Strome would not be a throw-in, either. He is a center, which is exactly what Detroit would be losing in Larkin. In 13 games this season, Strome has three goals and nine assists with a plus-3 rating. He is 29 years old and would slot into Detroit’s top six immediately. That is the shape of a Capitals deal: Protas as the young piece Detroit has been hunting, Strome as the salary that makes the cap work, and Washington deciding whether Larkin is worth breaking up its middle to get.

item.title: European giants set to battle in the race for £70m-rated Tottenham Hotspur star
item.description: European giants set to battle in the race for £70m-rated Tottenham Hotspur star Pedro Porro Transfer Latest: Tottenham Set Huge Price Amid Barcelona and Real Madrid Interest Pedro Porro has become one of the hottest names in the transfer market again, and with good reason. The Tottenham full-back has reached that stage in a top player’s career where admiration quickly turns into speculation, and speculation starts to carry a price tag all of its own. According to Sport , both Barcelona and Real Madrid have been linked with the Spain international after his impressive rise and his strong displays on the international stage. It is easy to see why. Porro brings thrust, personality and technical quality from right-back, and in a modern game that values width and invention from deep, those qualities are worth a fortune. The noise around his future has been amplified by the player himself, even if only gently. In comments that will have travelled quickly across Spain, Porro admitted, “It’s my country and I like the league. Right now it would be very unfair to talk about other things than my club because I have a contract, but obviously I’d love to return to Spain, it excites me a lot.” It was honest, measured and revealing all at once. Barcelona and Real Madrid alerted by Porro stance There is always a difference between interest and intent, and Porro appeared keen to make that clear. When asked about the prospect of representing Barcelona or Real Madrid, he did not take sides. Instead, he presented himself as a player capable of fitting anywhere, which is the sort of answer that keeps every option alive without setting fire to the present. He also attempted to cool the story with the line, “There is interest, they ask about your situation, but no real interest.” That may ease some of the frenzy, but it does not make the subject disappear. At this level, clubs often circle long before they strike, and information-gathering is part of the first movement in any serious pursuit. Photo: IMAGO Tottenham valuation makes Pedro Porro deal difficult The more significant obstacle appears to be Tottenham themselves. The report suggests the north London club would demand between £70m and £80m for Porro, a figure that instantly shifts this from an enticing possibility to a deeply complicated negotiation. Even for Barcelona and Real Madrid, that is premium money for a full-back, however polished and proven he may be. It is not hard to understand why Tottenham would hold firm. Elite right-backs are scarce, Porro is in his prime, and his contract runs until June 2031 after a renewal before the World Cup. That length of deal gives Spurs strength, control and time. It tells any suitor that they will not be bullied, rushed or drawn into a discount. LaLiga return may have to wait For all the romance of a return to Spain, this feels like a story that may require patience. item.description: Former NFL quarterback and current football analyst Dan Orlovsky has given Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix some major recognition following his latest impressive performance against the Kansas City Chiefs. Speaking on ESPN’s First Take on Monday, Orlovsky declared Nix the most clutch quarterback in the NFL after leading Denver to a dramatic 28-24 comeback victory in Week 8. “Bo Nix is the most clutch quarterback in the NFL,” Orlovsky said. “He’s 25-3 when trailing since the start of 2025, that’s outrageous, he’s the most clutch guy in ball right now.” “Bo Nix is the most clutch quarterback in the NFL.” 😤 @danorlovsky7 gives praise to the Broncos QB after their win against the Chiefs. https://t.co/exRklWwJwk — First Take (@FirstTake) November 2, 2026 The praise comes after another remarkable comeback from the third-year quarterback, who continues to establish himself as one of the league’s most reliable performers in high-pressure situations. MORE: NFL contenders & pretenders after Week 8 Nix continues to deliver in clutch moments Nov 1, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) passes the ball against the Kansas City Chiefs during the second quarter at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Despite trailing Kansas City by 11 points in the fourth quarter, Nix led Denver’s offense on a comeback that secured another important divisional victory. The performance marked the 25-year-old’s 15th career game-winning drive and his 12th fourth-quarter comeback since entering the NFL in 2024. Both totals are tied for the most by any quarterback in NFL history through his first three seasons. Nix finished Sunday’s contest completing 20 of 32 pass attempts for 222 yards and two touchdowns. His efforts helped the Broncos secure their fourth consecutive victory while handing the Chiefs their second straight loss. Beyond his ability to deliver in important moments, Nix has also been taking care of the football. He has now gone five consecutive games without throwing an interception, tying for the second-longest streak in Broncos franchise history and marking the team’s longest such run since Case Keenum accomplished the feat in 2018. Nix has attempted 164 consecutive passes without an interception, making it the second time in his career that he has surpassed 160 attempts without a turnover through the air.
